title: Bearing turns written coding rules into checks after each agent turn
friendlyTitle: Bearing checks whether coding agents follow written team rules
summary: Bearing is a new linter that evaluates code diffs against natural-language conventions from files such as AGENTS.md and skills. It uses the Jev decision model to return structured judgments and probabilities after an agent completes a turn.
friendlySummary: Bearing reads plain-English coding rules and checks an agent’s code changes after each step. It can look for problems that ordinary code linters do not understand.
whyItMatters: Many important engineering rules are too contextual for traditional static analysis. Turning team guidance into frequent review checks could catch architecture, testing and user-copy drift earlier, though model-based judgments still need calibration and oversight.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Teams can give agents clearer guardrails and catch mistakes sooner. Because the checks also use AI, people should still review important decisions.
